$what-an-entry-is: A licence for ONE test, keyed by its TEST NAME, to fail without failing CI.
$rules: A failure that is NOT on this list fails the gate. That is the whole point of the gate.
The list may only SHRINK. If a listed test PASSES, the gate fails until the entry is deleted — so a fix and its deletion land in the same PR.

Every reason must name a mechanism: what the test binds, spawns, writes, reads, or assumes about the machine or the calendar. The loader REJECTS the words 'flaky', 'intermittent' and 'unstable' — a failure with no named mechanism is indistinguishable from a real regression, which is how a real regression hides.

A test that is genuinely nondeterministic cannot satisfy the shrink-only ratchet, so it may set "nondeterministic": true to opt out of it. That is a bigger licence and costs more: such an entry MUST carry "tracking" (the issue where the defect is being fixed) and "expires" (an ISO date after which the gate fails). A quarantine with no meter is a parking space.

$fields.test: the test name exactly as the runner reports it — this is the key
$fields.file: repo-relative path, for the reader; cross-checked whenever the runner reports file attribution
$fields.reason: the mechanism — at least 40 characters, and not the word 'flaky'
$fields.nondeterministic: optional; true opts the entry out of the shrink-only ratchet
$fields.tracking: required when nondeterministic — the issue tracking the fix
$fields.expires: required when nondeterministic — ISO date after which this entry fails the gate

entries.reason: Whole-FILE timeout, not a single assertion: withDaemon's teardown sends SIGTERM and waits 3s, which is not enough, so devflow-watch daemons survive their tests holding the file process's stdio handles open and node can never exit that file. Observed locally with two daemons still alive 8+ minutes after their tests ended; on CI it surfaces as 'test timed out after 180000ms'. Licensing this entry licenses losing that whole file's coverage until issue #93 lands.

entries.test: PTY-2: dispatch("echo hello") returns stdout="hello\n", exit_code=0, status="done"
entries.reason: Linux-only, deterministic. readline's bracketed-paste pair ESC[?2004h / ESC[?2004l is emitted around every line read by the bash that ships on ubuntu-latest (readline >= 8.1). wrappers/bash.cjs initLines('pty') sends stty -echo, which suppresses the tty driver's echo and nothing readline writes itself, so the sequences land between the BEGIN and DELIM sentinels and become part of captured stdout. macOS bash 3.2 has no such mode, which is why no developer here has seen it. Product bug, not a test bug — see issue #95.

entries.test: PTY-4: dispatch("echo err 1>&2") captures stderr separately via sentinel protocol
entries.reason: Same mechanism as PTY-2: readline bracketed-paste sequences (ESC[?2004h / ESC[?2004l) from the ubuntu-latest bash land inside the sentinel-fenced capture region, so the captured stderr is the escape pair rather than empty. Deterministic on Linux, absent on macOS bash 3.2. Issue #95.

entries.test: PTY-5: env preserved across two dispatches (export FOO=bar; echo $FOO -> "bar\n")
entries.reason: Same mechanism as PTY-2: readline bracketed-paste sequences from the ubuntu-latest bash pollute the fenced capture region, so stdout is ESC[?2004h ESC[?2004l around 'bar' rather than 'bar\n'. Deterministic on Linux, absent on macOS bash 3.2. Issue #95.

Same mechanism as PTY-2: readline bracketed-paste sequences from the ubuntu-latest bash bracket the multi-line output inside the fenced capture region. Deterministic on Linux, absent on macOS bash 3.2. Issue #95.

entries.test: DL-5: PTY mode: attachDataListener fires on dispatch chunks
entries.reason: Same mechanism as PTY-2: the data listener receives the readline bracketed-paste sequences from the ubuntu-latest bash alongside the payload, so the chunk is not 'ptydata\n'. Deterministic on Linux, absent on macOS bash 3.2. Issue #95.

Runs only where pwsh is on PATH, which ubuntu-latest has and a typical macOS checkout does not, so it skips locally and runs in CI. `exit 7` inside `& { ... }` terminates the whole `pwsh -Command` host before the __DFW_END_ sentinel line executes, so stdout is empty — the test's own comment asserts the opposite premise. PW-8 (same shape, no exit) passes, so pwsh itself is fine. Decide whether wrappers/powershell.cjs can report a non-zero exit code at all before touching the assertion. Issue #95.

$why-the-key-is-the-name: Not file::name, which was the first design. node 22's junit reporter emits no testcase file attribute and node 25's does, so a file-based key resolves differently on a developer's machine and on the runner — the list would appear to shrink locally and silently fail to match in CI. The name is identical on every version. The cost is ambiguity, and it is paid explicitly: the gate FAILS when a listed name matches more than one test in the run.
$environment: This list describes the GATE's environment: ubuntu-latest + node 22, as pinned in .github/workflows/test.yml. Six of these entries are platform-specific and PASS or SKIP on macOS, so a developer running scripts/ci-unit-gate.cjs locally will see the shrink-only ratchet complain that they 'PASSED this run'. That is expected: the gate is a CI gate, and the ratchet is evaluated against CI.
